properties.name: spring.supabase.anon-key
properties.description: The project's anon (publishable) key: sent as `apikey` with every call, and as the bearer token while nobody is signed in. It is meant to be public; what it may read and write is decided by the database's row-level security.

properties.name: spring.supabase.auth.auto-refresh
properties.description: Whether the access token is refreshed in the background before it expires. Without it, it is refreshed when the next call needs it.

properties.name: spring.supabase.auth.enabled
properties.description: Whether the starter plugs Supabase Auth into Spring Security: on a server its tokens are accepted as bearer tokens, in a client application `SupabaseAuth` signs users in.

properties.name: spring.supabase.auth.issuer
properties.description: The issuer of the project's tokens (their `iss`). Default: `<url>/auth/v1`.

properties.name: spring.supabase.auth.jwt-secret
properties.description: The JWT secret of a project that still signs its tokens with HS256 (the legacy secret). Server only: with it tokens can be forged for any user. Projects with signing keys (ES256, RS256) leave it unset and the server reads the project's public keys.

properties.name: spring.supabase.auth.persist-session
properties.description: Whether the session is kept across restarts (in the application's secret store when it has one).

properties.name: spring.supabase.auth.redirect-urls
properties.description: The addresses a login through a provider, a magic link or a password reset may come back to. A redirect to any other address is refused before the request is made. The first one is the default.

properties.name: spring.supabase.auth.refresh-margin
properties.description: How long before its expiry an access token counts as expired.

properties.name: spring.supabase.cache.shared
properties.description: The caches whose entries are the same for every user. Every other cache keeps the entries of each user (and of the anon key and of the service role) apart, because with row-level security one call answers differently per user.

properties.name: spring.supabase.connect-timeout
properties.description: How long the connection of Realtime may take to open. The HTTP calls go through the application's `HttpTransport` bean, whose own connect timeout applies to them; [timeout] limits each of them as a whole.

properties.name: spring.supabase.db.max-rows
properties.description: The most rows the REST API returns in one answer: the project's "Max rows" (API settings), `max_rows` of the local stack. An answer that long may have been cut there, without any sign of it, so a query that asks for more (or for everything) reads on in further calls, ordered by the id. Set it to the project's value when that one was changed: with a larger number here a cut answer is taken for whole.

properties.name: spring.supabase.db.rls
properties.description: As whom SQL runs. See [SupabaseRls].

properties.name: spring.supabase.db.schema
properties.description: The schema the REST API reads and writes (PostgREST's `Accept-Profile` / `Content-Profile`). Default: the API's own default (`public`).

properties.name: spring.supabase.db.url
properties.description: The PostgreSQL address of the project (`postgresql://postgres:<password>@db.<ref>.supabase.co:5432/postgres`, or a pooler's). When it is set, the repositories use SQL over it (transactions, `@Lock`, SQL `@Query` and `JdbcClient` work); when it is not (the default), they use the project's REST API (PostgREST), where those do not exist.

properties.name: spring.supabase.functions.region
properties.description: The region the functions run in (the `x-region` header); the nearest one when not set.

properties.name: spring.supabase.functions.timeout
properties.description: How long a function may take. Default: `spring.supabase.timeout`.

properties.name: spring.supabase.rate-limit.function
properties.description: The database function an acquisition calls; the one of the package's `sql/rate_limit.sql` unless that was renamed.

properties.name: spring.supabase.realtime.heartbeat-interval
properties.description: How often the connection says it is alive.

properties.name: spring.supabase.realtime.max-message-size
properties.description: The largest message read from Realtime (a change of a row can be 1 MB, a broadcast 3 MB); a larger one closes the connection.

properties.name: spring.supabase.realtime.timeout
properties.description: How long a join or a message waits for its answer.

properties.name: spring.supabase.service-role-key
properties.description: The project's service role (secret) key, used only inside `SupabaseCredentials.asServiceRole`. It passes row-level security: keep it on a server. An application that ships it (a Flutter app) is warned at build time and at startup, since whoever has the app has the key.

properties.name: spring.supabase.storage.signed-url-expiry
properties.description: How long a signed URL is valid when the call does not say.

properties.name: spring.supabase.timeout
properties.description: How long a call may take, the answer's body included. Downloads and uploads of Storage are not limited by it.

properties.name: spring.supabase.url
properties.description: The project's address (`https://<ref>.supabase.co`, or the local stack's `http://127.0.0.1:54321`). Every service is called under it (`/rest/v1`, `/auth/v1`, `/storage/v1`, `/functions/v1`, `/realtime/v1`), and a key or a token is only ever sent to it.

values.description: As the user of `spring.supabase.db.url` (usually `postgres`, which passes row-level security). The default.

As the current user: every transaction sets the role `authenticated` (or `anon` when nobody is signed in) and the user's token claims, so the policies of row-level security apply with transactions and locks too.
